De haber acertado en esa tirada, hubiera vencido a Wu Yize y disputado su primera final de un campeonato del Mundo. "Tuve mis oportunidades y, para ser honesto, las desaproveché por completo. Cuando fallas un tiro así, no mereces ganar. Tuve muchísimas oportunidades para ganar", comentó entonces Allen. Wu ganaría luego la final para reafirmar el emergente poderío chino con el taco en la mano. Desde entonces no se había vuelto a poner ante una mesa de billar. Regresó hace dos días en el Open de Irlanda del Norte tras haber permanecido 10 semanas en una clínica de salud mental. Perdió en primera ronda ante Jordan Brown. Tras la derrota, en una entrevista reconoció que pensaba en dejar el snooker: "Los últimos tres meses han sido realmente muy difíciles y el simple hecho de estar aquí hoy ya es un logro. Para mí, no se trataba del resultado ni del rendimiento, sino de disfrutar de la experiencia de jugar contra uno de mis mejores amigos en uno de mis recintos favoritos, en uno de mis torneos favoritos. No voy a anunciar mi retirada ahora mismo tras una derrota, pero es algo que llevo tiempo considerando y algo tiene que cambiar en las próximas seis semanas, antes del Campeonato del Reino Unido, para que yo pueda presentarme" Allen usó luego sus redes sociales para confirmar lo que dijo en esta entrevista e ir más allá. Contó que había permanecido ingresado en una clínica de salud mental. "Recibí el alta para poder intentar jugar en Belfast. Se lo debía a mi familia, en particular a mi hija, para que me viera jugar en lo que podría ser la última vez…", escribe Allen. "También se lo debía a los aficionados que me han apoyado durante mis 21 años en el circuito y a World Snooker, que han sido increíbles desde el primer día en todo esto, en particular Simon Brownell y Neil Tomkins, que han mantenido el contacto regularmente, incluso Simon visitándome en la clínica", prosigue Allen. El ganador de 12 títulos del circuito, entre ellos el Campeonato del Reino Unido de 2022, contó lo mal que lo ha pasado: "No estoy bien, pero he estado mucho peor en los últimos meses de lo que vieron ayer. Literalmente no veía un futuro en nada. Mi hija me mantuvo adelante, los terapeutas, el personal y todos los demás pacientes fueron increíbles y me ayudaron a pasar por algunos días realmente oscuros". "Ahora veo la luz que antes no podía ver. También sé que no sucederá de la noche a la mañana. Estoy progresando. Mi lucha y determinación en la mesa siempre han estado ahí para que todos lo vean. Ahora necesito mostrar esas mismas cualidades de lucha fuera de la mesa durante un tiempo", comentó Allen.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Dragon Lee's New Contract & Jordynne Grace, Ilja Dragunov Talks Pay Cut Speculation
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Amid his recent run of entertaining matches on Raw, Dragon Lee is reportedly remaining with WWE for the long haul.

According to PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ), Lee agreed to a new contract with WWE, and it is believed to be five years in length.

PWInsider added that Lee's previous deal had been set to expire at some point in October.

A 31-year-old Superstar from Mexico, Lee has been with WWE since 2022, following stints with CMLL, AAA, New Japan Pro-Wrestling, Ring of Honor and AEW.

Lee held the NXT North American Championship, WWE Speed Championship and World Tag Team Championship one time each, but he is arguably enjoying his greatest run of success right now.

For much of 2026, Lee has been in the Intercontinental Championship mix, challenging Penta for the title in a singles match in March and as part of a six-man ladder match at WrestleMania 42.

Since Chad Gable beat Penta for the IC title at SummerSlam, Lee has challenged him for the championship on multiple occasions as well.

That included a singles bout on the Sept. 14 episode of Raw in Mexico City, and a Triple Threat that also involved Rey Mysterio this week on Raw.

Despite falling short in each instance, Lee has gained a great deal of equity with the viewing audience thanks to his spectacular performances in those matches.

Now that Lee is reportedly locked in for five years, it may only be a matter of time before he breaks through and becomes IC champ.

Latest on WWE's Reported Creative Plans for Jordynne Grace

New details have emerged regarding Jordynne Grace's status amid her lengthy absence from WWE programming.

According to Fightful Select (h/t WrestlePurists ), there were plans in place as of last month for Grace to form a tag team with Ivy Nile.

It was reportedly anticipated that WWE would begin teasing the tag team at some point in September by airing vignettes that Grace and Nile had filmed.

Despite that, Grace has remained absent from WWE TV, as she last wrestled on SmackDown back in April, and last wrestled a match of any kind on Main Event in June.

WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t WrestlePurists ) reported that the reason for Grace's absence is that she is "not in the creative plans."

It was also noted by WrestleVotes that Grace recently took part in a fitness competition, so it was speculated that it could have extended her absence beyond what was initially planned, although that has not been confirmed.

Grace, 30, officially signed with WWE in January 2025 following a hugely successful run in TNA that saw her hold the Knockouts World Championship three times.

Although Grace has yet to hold a title in WWE, she has impressed from an in-ring perspective when given the opportunity thanks to her combination of strength and athleticism.

Teaming up with Nile could be exactly what she needs in order to get back in the mix and showcase her skills, but for now, that plan appears to be in a holding pattern.

AEW's Dragunov Addresses WWE Contract Offer

Ilja Dragunov declined to get into specifics regarding the contract offer WWE made him before he decided to leave and sign with AEW.

During an interview this week on the Ariel Helwani Show (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), Dragunov was asked about his contract situation and negotiations with WWE prior to his departure:

Dragunov noted that the talks "did not lead anywhere," and when asked if WWE wanted him to take a pay cut, he said, "Did they offer me a pay cut? To be honest, I am too much of a discreet businessman to talk about these kinds of things."

The Mad Dragon added, "Everything I can say is there was nothing I felt was satisfying and nothing that gave me the perspective of, like, 'Okay, I must stick with here.'"

Dragunov, 33, was under contract with WWE since 2019 before recently becoming a free agent.

He held both the NXT United Kingdom Championship and NXT Championship before getting called up to the main roster and becoming a one-time United States champion.

However, Dragunov was kept off television for months after last wrestling in April, apparently due to the fact that he was on an expiring contract.

He and WWE were unable to reach an agreement on a new deal, which paved the way for him to join AEW, making his debut last weekend at WrestleDream.

Wednesday night on Dynamite, Dragunov will compete in his AEW debut match against "Speedball" Mike Bailey.

articles.title: NHL Teams Tease Hometown Remix Uniforms in Photos Ahead of Official Release
articles.summary: The NHL is teasing new specialty jerseys for the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
The NHL is teasing new specialty jerseys for the 2026-27 season.

Teams released ciphers Wednesday hinting at Hometown Remix uniforms that will be introduced later this season.

Quick Predictions on Biggest Storylines 🔮

First Star Scouting's Brandon Holmes shared a list of some estimated answers to the ciphers.

The Edmonton Oilers were later decoded as "Oil Country After Midnight." The New York Rangers were the only club that did not join in on the initial drop.

The NHL announced in August teams would be introducing a new Hometown Remix look "that uniquely and authentically celebrates the fans, city, and local culture of each team."

Some teams have seemingly offered hints at what could potentially be parts of their new specialty uniforms with new looks at practice, including black pants for the Edmonton Oilers and navy helmets for the Nashville Predators.

Fanatics took over as the NHL's official supplier ahead of the 2024-25 season on a deal that runs through 2035.

The apparel brand has instituted similar programs in the past with the NBA's City Edition jerseys and MLB's City Connect uniforms.

The NHL most recently ran a specialty jersey promotion under Adidas under the Reverse Retro collection, collections from which dropped in 2020 and 2022.

Los Angeles Kings chief revenue officer Darren Abbott said in August (h/t Icethetics ) he thought each team was mandated to wear the Hometown Remix jerseys at least seven times.

At least some full Hometown Remix jerseys will be revealed within the next two weeks, according to uniform schedules released ahead of the season by clubs.

The Buffalo Sabres have already confirmed the club's sweater will make its first appearance Nov. 4 against the Ottawa Senators, while the New York Islanders will debut their own Hometown Remix look Nov. 5 against the Carolina Hurricanes.

The St. Louis Blues and Winnipeg Jets will each feature their new looks Nov. 17 against the Anaheim Ducks and Ottawa Senators, respectively.

The full release of the Hometown Remix uniforms will eventually be accompanied by the release of replica jerseys and other apparel, according to the NHL.

articles.title: Coki Nieto: "¿Mi estilo? Creo que va a durar poco en el pádel"
articles.standfirst: El revés madrileño se sincera sobre el futuro del deporte y su actual momento en MARCA X3
articles.summary: El revés madrileño se sincera sobre el futuro del deporte y su actual momento en MARCA X3
articles.body: Coki Nieto (Madrid, 1999) es uno de los referentes de Premier Padel en las últimas temporadas. A base de trabajo y con un estilo cada vez menos habitual en este deporte, el revés español se ha ganado un hueco entre los mejores del mundo y, aunque en esta temporada ha tenido algunos problemas físicos, ha logrado brillar en varios torneos. Durante la emisión del último programa de MARCA X3, el madrileño valoró su momento actual con Mike Yanguas, su anterior etapa con Jon Sanz y cómo ve la tan importante cita en la que está convocado: el Mundial. Pregunta: ¿Cómo está, Coki? Respuesta: Muy bien, encantado de estar aquí. Muchas gracias por la invitación y feliz. P: ¿Cómo está llevando esta temporada con tantos torneos y tanta intensidad? R: Difícil, porque al principio tuve una lesión que no me permitió hacer una buena pretemporada y los primeros torneos a lo mejor no salieron como quería, pero a medida que ha ido pasando el año y la temporada creo que me encuentro mejor. Ahora, con Mike, yo creo que estamos jugando bien y a ver si podemos terminar el año de una buena manera. P: ¿Qué le pasó en ese momento? Se perdió la Hexagon Cup, el primer torneo del año... ¿Qué le pasó? R: Sí, tenía varias exhibiciones antes del primer torneo y me perdí la Reserve Cup, me perdí la Hexagon, luego el primer torneo de la temporada. Tuve un ligamento del codo que no me permitía pegarle fuerte. Sí que podía jugar, pero a la hora de pegar a la pelota sentía un pinchazo. He estado varios meses hasta marzo jugando con un poco de dolor y luego con ejercicios de gimnasio y adaptación he podido mejorar y ahora estoy bien. P: Empezó el año con Jon, que era una pareja que ya se dio en el pasado y tuvieron muy buenos torneos, pero quizás no tan buenos resultados como en su primera etapa. ¿Qué pasó? ¿Cómo valora esa etapa con Jon? R: La gente nos ponía más responsabilidad de la que teníamos, porque al final salíamos de pareja cinco. Tenemos muy buenos recuerdos de la primera etapa, pero al final lo que hicimos fue ganar un Master Final, que obviamente es muy bueno; ganamos un P2 en Burdeos, que faltaban las mejores parejas; pero luego en la primera etapa hicimos muchos cuartos de final. Y este año igual, saliendo de pareja cinco, que te encuentras en cuartos de final a parejas duras, sí que es verdad que ha habido partidos que no hemos competido, pero bueno, yo creo que hemos hecho buenos resultados, alguna derrota que no tocaba, pero bueno. Yo me voy con buena sensación con Jon, creo que jugamos bien, podríamos haberlo hecho mejor seguro, pero bueno, contento con Jon. P: Sin haber hecho tampoco unos resultados increíbles, pero haciendo muy buenos resultados, ¿por qué deciden separar la pareja? R: A Jon le llama Stupa y él decide jugar con él y no me queda otra que aceptarlo y buscar compañero. Fue decisión de Jon y es verdad que yo confiaba mucho en el proyecto con él. Yo creo que él también confiaba, pero bueno, al final Stupa también es un gran jugador y no me queda otra que aceptarlo. P: ¿Regularía los cambios de pareja en el pádel? R: Bueno, yo sinceramente no era partidario de regularlo porque al final si te lesionas o se lesiona tu compañero es complicado, porque es un deporte de parejas y hay un efecto dominó por el que se rompen muchas parejas. Entonces, creo que es complicado. Ojalá se pueda regular de alguna manera. Creo que sería bueno para el deporte, porque al final la gente se identifica con parejas o le gusta una pareja u otra y yo creo que sería bueno. P: Y después de dejarlo con Jon, primer torneo con Yanguas en Premier y hacen final, ¿se lo esperaba? R: No lo esperaba, la verdad, no te voy a mentir. Porque el año pasado sí que hicimos buenos resultados con Mike, hicimos 12 o 13 semifinales, no me acuerdo cuántas, y no conseguíamos llegar a ninguna final. Y este año con Mike se dio muy bien ese primer torneo, íbamos ganando partidos, en cuartos de final hicimos un partido perfecto y la verdad es que creo que jugamos a un gran nivel. La final se escapó por poquito, pero creo que jugamos a un gran nivel. P: ¿Ha cambiado algo con respecto a su primera etapa? Porque lo hicieron muy bien pero no llegaron a ninguna final y el primer torneo van y hacen final. ¿Ha cambiado algo o es más fruto de las circunstancias? R: No creo que haya cambiado nada, yo creo que seguimos jugando más o menos igual que el año pasado. Es verdad que el año pasado tuvimos muchos partidos en los que estábamos cerca de la final y no se dio y este año, la primera de cambio que nos hemos juntado, nos salió un partido perfecto contra Agus y Arturo en cuartos de final. La verdad que en las semifinales era partido duro, pero no es una pareja como Galán y Chingotto o como Arturo y Tapia, que son la uno y la dos y tienes que jugar perfecto. Sabemos que era una buena oportunidad, salimos al 100% y conseguimos esa final tan ansiada. P: Es uno de los jugadores que más ha evolucionado con respecto a años anteriores, ¿qué ha cambiado en su juego, qué ha cambiado en usted para verse asentado entre los mejores del mundo? R: Creo sobre todo que ha sido un cambio más mental que de juego. Creo que de juego también he evolucionado, pero yo creo que el cambio que más he notado ha sido mentalmente, intentar entrar en pista sabiendo o queriendo ganar ese partido y creo que es lo que más noto. Y tener más confianza sobre todo en mí mismo. P: Hay muchísimos jugadores también que desean estar en esos puestos en los que está, ¿qué le diferencia del resto? ¿Qué le ha hecho llegar a estar tan arriba? R: Es una buena pregunta, yo creo que soy un jugador muy sólido, un jugador muy sólido que nunca da una bola por perdida y yo creo que soy un 7 siempre, no tengo golpes que sean muy buenos pero tampoco creo que tenga golpes que sean muy malos. Entonces, yo creo que siempre me he rodeado bien. He tenido buenos compañeros y yo creo que siempre intento jugar a un nivel muy regular, nunca soy un 10, nunca soy un 2. Eso es lo que me hace ser constante y estar arriba. P: Dice que tienes un estilo muy sólido y en un pádel que cada vez es más vertical, cada vez más agresivo, ¿cree que su estilo va a seguir teniendo cabida en el futuro? Porque pasan los años y sigue estando ahí. R: Yo creo que cada vez vamos a ir para abajo, yo creo que va a durar poquito, este tipo de jugadores ya se nota y ya se ve que cada vez hay menos jugadores que son más bajitos o ya los derechas cada vez son más grandes y para que un jugador de las características de Chingotto, de las mías o de las de Di Nenno o Bergamini yo creo que van a tener que ser muy buenos para poder seguir. Sobre todo por el camino que está llevando el circuito, que es cada vez hacia un pádel más rápido y más vertical. P: ¿Se plantea, por ejemplo, el cambio a la derecha en algún momento? R: Me gustaría, no te voy a mentir, yo creo que en un futuro me gustaría. Sobre todo porque siento que al revés me estoy quedando un poco... no atascado, pero noto que los demás vienen físicamente como aviones, son muy grandes, le pegan muy bien y entonces pues intentar cambiar a la derecha y hacer una buena adaptación e intentar rodearme de alguien que le pegue creo que sería interesante. P: ¿Qué tendría que cambiar para jugar a la derecha? Porque es un camino que por ejemplo ya probó Paquito, que no le salió bien, ¿cómo lo haría para que saliera bien? R: Es difícil. Paco hizo un cambio en mitad de temporada, así que yo creo que sería un cambio que tendría que hacer con mucho tiempo, una buena pretemporada y que los resultados no serían de un día para otro. Habría que jugar muchos partidos. Un año yo creo de adaptación y yo creo que no se sabe si saldrá bien o saldrá mal, pero bueno, adaptarse, poder jugar a la derecha creo que es importante y como te digo, rodearse de alguien que gane los puntos para yo poder trabajar y ayudarle a él. P: También año a año se va marcando objetivos y los va superando. Antes quería entrar entre las ocho, de repente entra entre las cuatro. A futuro, ¿cuáles son los objetivos de Coki Nieto? R: Siempre me había puesto de objetivos llegar a las ocho mejores parejas, nunca me hubiera imaginado el año pasado estar de pareja cuatro y aguantar todo el año. Es lo que te decía antes, que creo que mentalmente he mejorado y ha sido importante para cumplir mis objetivos. Ahora yo creo que es más seguir disfrutando del pádel, aguantar realmente el mayor número de tiempo posible entre las ocho mejores parejas que creo que cada vez está más duro y sería buena señal. P: Una de las cosas que dice su compañero Mike es que usted es uno de los jugadores más infravalorados, creo que cada vez se le valora más, pero... ¿se sigue considerando como uno de los más infravalorados o nota que cada vez le quiere más la gente? R: No sé, yo tengo mi público. Creo que el jugador amateur se relaciona con mi juego, mi estilo de juego, porque no es real lo que hace Tapia o lo que hace Augsburger. La gente amateur no lo puede hacer, entonces yo creo que a lo mejor se fijan un poco más en mi juego que es más de hacer bandeja, de trabajar mucho más el punto. Creo que por eso tengo mi público, no me considero infravalorado, la gente tiene gustos y a lo mejor gusto un poco menos, pero yo estoy feliz, no tengo problema. P: ¿Y este año, qué objetivo se marca? Ya no queda tanto pero ¿qué objetivo se marca? R: Creo que es ya un poco adelantado, me refiero a que el año está ya avanzado, estaría bien entrar entre las cuatro mejores parejas, creo que con Mike tenemos nivel para hacerlo, también depende mucho de los cuadros, también de los rivales, creo que sería un objetivo ambicioso pero creo que es real, y si no, pues entrar entre los 16 mejores jugadores para jugar el Master. P: Y una de las fechas más importantes en el calendario es el Mundial, ¿cómo lo ve? ¿Quién cree que es el favorito? R: Igualado, 50-50. Al final es un partido si se da todo bien, que esperemos que sí, y podamos llegar a la final. Yo creo que es 50-50, porque los jugadores que tiene Argentina contra los que tiene España son muy buenos, entonces ya ahí se decide el día que tenga uno y el día que tenga otro. Depende de eso. P: Precisamente en el de 2024 vivió un contraste de sensaciones: ganar su punto con Arturo haciendo un partidazo, y luego perder la final, ¿cómo fue para usted haber hecho tan buen papel y después que perdiera el equipo? R: Fue bastante duro porque yo antes de jugar pensaba que mi partido era el más complicado, o sea que si yo sacaba mi partido uno de los dos después íbamos a conseguir sacarlo. Se dio totalmente al revés, jugué con Arturo, jugamos un partidazo, pudimos ganar y luego yo creo que de 10 eliminatorias ganamos 9. Para mí, yo pienso eso. Creo que ellos compitieron muy bien, Tino y Leo jugaron espectacular, el partido de Chingotto y Tapia también podían haberlo ganado Galán y Lebrón tranquilamente. Fue un año de agua fría totalmente, porque yo al salir del partido pensaba que teníamos muchas opciones. P: Y este año, poniendo que es uno de los 6 que juega, ¿con quién le gustaría compartir pista? Porque ya ganó con Coello, ha jugado con Jon, con Yanguas, también está Lebrón... ¿con quién le gustaría compartir pista en caso de un punto? R: Con Coello sin duda. Te hace la vida mucho más fácil. Con Coello aparte, mentalmente yo hace dos años estaba muy nervioso para jugar, y él me tranquilizaba. Era como un padre y tenía 20 años. P: ¿Es posiblemente el complemento perfecto a su estilo de juego? R: Vamos, totalmente. Para cualquiera yo creo. Le viene bien a cualquier tipo de juego, pero a mí especialmente, que me falta pegada y definición, yo creo que más todavía. P: ¿Y de Argentina, contra qué pareja le gustaría enfrentarse? R: Si al final te tiene que tocar alguien, da igual. Te digo que jugando con Arturo, cualquiera. P: Y en un circuito que está creciendo tanto, con el pádel, con un deporte que está también expandiéndose tanto por el mundo, ¿qué cree que le falta para dar el siguiente paso? R: Creo que es un deporte que está creciendo a nivel mundial y es importante que se estructure bien todo el tipo de torneos. Sí que se están haciendo muchos campeonatos en todas las zonas del mundo, pero creo que falta cierta organización a la hora de reparto de puntos, reparto de torneos en ciertas ciudades, ciertos países... Creo que se está haciendo demasiado rápido, que es mejor estructurarlo un poco mejor, ir un pelín más lento y yo creo que eso va a llegar más lejos. P: También es importante cuidar la imagen de los jugadores. En el circuito, ¿quién es el más puntilloso, el que más cuida su imagen o quizás el más presumido? R: Presumido, no sé. El que mejor cuida la imagen, sin duda, yo te diría Arturo, que para mí lo hace muy bien. Todo lo que es alrededor de su imagen lo hace muy bien. Y el más presumido te diría... Jon. Es muy presumido. P: Y siendo uno de los grandes referentes del circuito, con tanta exposición en la tele, tanta exposición también en redes sociales, ¿se cuida mucho su imagen? R: Creo que nos cuidamos todos ya mucho la imagen. Al final, como salimos en la tele, en YouTube, en los partidos, yo intento cuidarme mucho la imagen. Siempre llevo mi afeitadora Philips, intento ir bien afeitado, así que bueno, creo que a medida que va creciendo el deporte, se interesan más medios de comunicación, entonces es importante cuidarnos.

articles.title: Giants cut a back, but Cam Skattebo still has work to do
articles.summary: The Giants finally removed a name from their crowded backfield. Now I want them to explain the remaining jobs and […]
articles.body:
The Giants finally removed a name from their crowded backfield. Now I want them to explain the remaining jobs and make the players earn them.

New York released Najee Harris on Tuesday , leaving Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary on the active roster. That gives the offense fewer backs to accommodate. It does not automatically make Skattebo a dependable lead runner.

Cam Skattebo's next Giants opportunity needs a standard

Skattebo has 294 yards on 81 carries, or 3.6 per attempt, with one rushing touchdown. Harris leaves behind 99 yards on 31 carries. Removing the less productive veteran is understandable, but neither set of results supports declaring the rushing attack fixed.

The concern with Skattebo extends beyond the average. His official season record includes four fumbles, with one lost. Four fumbles are not four turnovers, and there is no reason to inflate the criticism. There is plenty to address in the actual number.

He had no carries against New Orleans. Whatever the intended rotation, the practical outcome left the Giants ' leading rusher without a rushing attempt. Cutting Harris makes it harder to explain away another week in which a committee leaves an important player out of the running game entirely.

I'd give Skattebo a defined early assignment against Houston and use it to evaluate more than yardage. Does he protect the ball through contact? Does he take the available gain? Can the offense return to him after an unproductive series without abandoning the rest of the plan? Those are better questions than whether he receives a ceremonial first carry.

A smaller committee can still be a bad committee

Tracy and Singletary remain alternatives. If either executes better, the Giants should use him. The point of a clearer rotation is to make performance matter, not to guarantee Skattebo touches regardless of what follows.

Nor can a backfield transaction settle the blocking. Removing Harris doesn't improve a missed assignment up front or establish who will be available along the line this week. Skattebo's numbers are part of an offensive problem, not proof that every failed run belongs to him.

The Giants haven't announced a new feature-back role or established that any public comments caused the release. We should not invent either. What changed Tuesday is the personnel. What needs to change Sunday is the clarity: give Skattebo a real opportunity, keep alternatives involved for a reason and stop allowing the rotation itself to become another explanation for poor production.

The Eagles ' disappointing start could lead to more roster changes before the trade deadline.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler identified Philadelphia as a potential candidate for a smaller rebuild, reporting that the Eagles frequently come up in conversations about teams that could make moves. That possibility puts added weight on the upcoming stretch against Dallas, Washington, and the Giants . Philadelphia still has a chance to improve its position in the NFC East, but another run of losses would make it easier to justify prioritizing future assets.

I'll start with the Eagles. They come up most often regarding potential moves over the next few weeks. The Eagles are always active, and they could execute a mini-rebuild. Defensive end Moro Ojomo , a 2027 free agent, has strong trade value, so if Philadelphia isn't going to re-sign him, it could get compensatory pick value (or better) for him now. Woolen and wide receiver Hollywood Brown are players teams are watching. I'm not wholly convinced the Eagles will move a marquee name such as Saquon Barkley . But can they find a taker for guard Landon Dickerson , who appears disgruntled and remains on injured reserve ? The Eagles have been forced to reshape their once-vaunted offensive line on the fly, and that could facilitate moves. It's also worth noting that Philly is in the middle of a quarterback shake-up due to Jalen Hurts' absence, and recently acquired QB Joe Milton is a name to watch. articles.title: The Pelicans starter already on hot seat as he stares down monster matchups before Halloween
articles.summary: There is perhaps no tougher stress test to start the season than Yves Missi’s matchups through Halloween. Ivica Zubac, Jaren Jackson Jr., Nikola Jokic, and D...
articles.body:
There is perhaps no tougher stress test to start the season than Yves Missi 's matchups through Halloween. Ivica Zubac , Jaren Jackson Jr., Nikola Jokic , and Domantas Sabonis are waiting. Jokic gets two cracks at Missi in a five-day span. It is hardly an ideal welcome to a starting role for a 22-year-old still learning the game. For better or worse, these New Orleans Pelicans will quickly learn how much patience Jamahl Mosley has for growing pains .

Missi has the athleticism, length, and defensive instincts to become a legitimate postseason-playable center. The former Baylor standout averaged 9.1 points and 8.2 rebounds as a rookie before slipping to 5.7 points and 5.8 rebounds in a reduced role last season. Everyone expects the Cameroonian star to be in the starting lineup on Opening Night against the Indiana Pacers.

Still, Mosley has already established a new accountability system that could make any potential early struggles impossible to ignore.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I'm not doing 10-game sample sizes. I won't do that," Mosley told ClutchPoints. "We will break it down more into five-game segments, treating it like a series."

There is a delicate balance between holding a young player accountable and destroying his confidence. No one expects Missi to outperform Jokic, Sabonis, or Jackson to justify a starting role moving forward. That would be ridiculous, even with the front office hyping up Defensive Player of the Year goals.

The Halloween matchup against the Atlanta Hawks offers a potentially more manageable assignment, particularly if they run out Asa Newell more than Onyeka Okongwu. By then, Mosley will have completed his first five-game evaluation window. However, will Missi still be the unquestioned starter, or will the five have to be more matchup-dependent?

If Missi is consistently getting outmuscled, however, Mosley will need answers. EVP Joe Dumars and Mosley were clear about the postseason expectations during the Media Day sessions. So what's the fallback option?

Derik Queen offers a more creative offensive option at center. His passing, scoring instincts, and ability to facilitate could give the Pelicans a different dimension, particularly alongside Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III. However, shifting Queen into the starting lineup would create its own defensive concerns.

Karlo Matkovic is another possibility. His size and ability to stretch the floor could give Williamson additional room to operate, although he would face many of the same physical challenges against the West's elite centers. Herb Jones at the five has been effective in small sample sizes, but would be a break glass in case of emergency panic move.

None of those alternatives represents a perfect answer. That is precisely why Missi's development matters so much. Mosley cannot afford to abandon his young center after a handful of difficult matchups. Getting beaten by an MVP is not necessarily evidence of failure. Getting beaten repeatedly because of poor positioning, missed assignments, or a lack of physicality is a different conversation.

Zach Edey (Nov. 2), Jackson Jr. again (Nov. 4), then Rudy Gobert (Nov. 6) is a scary follow-up after the first evaluation period. Jokic (Nov. 14) comes back to the Smoothie King Center before turkeys are defrosting. Jalen Duren (Nov. 18), the Chet Holmgren /Aday Mara duo (Nov. 20), and Victor Wembanyama (Nov. 21) are up the next week, with the latter two being a road-road back-to-back.

Assistant coach Dale Osbourne explained during a pre-camp coaching clinic that 'Pray' is the game plan against Jokic. The rest is down to getting creative defensively. It's perhaps the only way Mosley's Pelicans keep up with the Play-In pack through Thanksgiving.

articles.title: Tyler Warren injury update from Colts practice is discouraging sign for Week 7
articles.summary: Tyler Warren's practice week is off to a bad start.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts were forced to operate without star tight end Tyler Warren in Week 6 and they are on track to do the same in Week 7.

The Colts hit the practice field for the first time this week on Wednesday, and when they did, Warren was not spotted among the participants.

"Colts who don't appear to be practicing today: Sauce Gardner, Justin Walley, Bryce Boettcher, Mooney Ward, Keenan Allen, Tyler Warren, Drew Ogletree, Anthony Gould, Matt Goncalves," Colts Roundtable's Jake Arthur reported.

We'll get final confirmation on Warren's Wednesday status when the Colts release their injury report later in the day.

Warren popped up on the injury report unexpectedly at the end of last week.

After practicing in full on Wednesday and Thursday, Warren injured his groin at practice on Friday and was given the questionable tag.

He was a game-time decision on Sunday, but Warren was ultimately inactive for the loss to the Tennessee Titans.

And it showed in Indy's offense, which was also without wide receiver Alec Pierce, who remains on injured reserve with his heel issue.

The Colts managed just 20 points against the Titans in the upset loss, and Indy decided to fire general manager Chris Ballard afterwards, a move that was long overdue.

How Colts will replace Tyler Warren if ruled out

It will take a village to replace an elite pass-catching tight end like Warren, but even a village probably won't be enough.

Last week, Will Mallory, Drew Ogletree and Mo Alie-Cox all got more run with Warren sidelined.

But that trio combined for just three catches for 21 yards, with Mallory tallying two grabs for 20 yards and Alie-Cox finishing with one catch for one yard.

Not that it needs to be said, but we'll say it anyway: fantasy football owners will have to look elsewhere for help this week if Warren doesn't suit up.

That said, there is still hope Warren can rebound during the week and play on Sunday.

After putting out their first injury report of the week Wednesday, the Colts will have two more practices on Thursday and Friday before their final injury report comes out on the latter day.

articles.body:
Michael Carrick has decided to withdraw Bruno Fernandes from the action against Como in the 66th minute.

Despite Manchester United trailing by three goals at the time of his departure, Carrick replaced his skipper with Joshua Zirkzee.

Fernandes hooked prematurely in Como clash

"That's a shock. It really is," reacted Glenn Hoddle on TNT Sports , to which main commentator Adam Summerton noted that Fernandes responded with a 'shake of the head' when making his way to the bench.

The Portugal star played 80 minutes in last week's defeat to Atletico Madrid, but other than that one outing, he has stayed on for the full 90 in every game he's started, so you can understand him being taken aback by the change.

Yet, Carrick did openly forewarn his players that game time was not by any means guaranteed if they were not performing at the level required, which Fernandes hasn't been as of late.

"This is not on Bruno, this line, but nobody is guaranteed a place in the team. Don't take that as me talking on Bruno, just in general. There's a level of performance, behaviour, understanding we need as a squad to perform.

"All the boys know that, they understand that, they've got their own standards and want to be at their best. That's pretty clear," said the manager last week.

How Fernandes has been faring as of late

Meanwhile, the 32-year-old is without a goal contribution in his last seven appearances in all competitions, including tonight.

Fans and pundits have pointed out that Fernandes is cutting a much more frustrated figure than usual, having seemingly grown accustomed to such lacklustre, repetitive results at the club.

Reports have suggested that he will be looking to move on in 2027, with his contract due to expire next June – though United have the option of extending his stay by an additional 12 months.

articles.summary: Juventus is struggling, and as anyone can imagine, this is probably the time when Luciano Spalletti is having sleepless nights as their manager. The gaffer h...
articles.body:
Juventus is struggling, and as anyone can imagine, this is probably the time when Luciano Spalletti is having sleepless nights as their manager. The gaffer has done his best, but in just one game when he was not on the touchline because of a ban, his team was well beaten by Lazio at home .

That 3-0 defeat hurts so much, as it showed that the players are not yet at the level he thought they had reached, and they continue to struggle for form. Juve is one of the top teams in the world, and they have to play better at home, so it is embarrassing that they could be beaten so badly by Lazio.

Spalletti has to find solutions, and Tuttomercatoweb says he is now thinking about changing his formation, and one of the main reasons is that he wants to accommodate Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade at the same time. The report says he is now thinking about trialling the 3-5-2 formation in his next game so that he can use both strikers, and that will also open up a chance for Lloyd Kelly to play more alongside Gleison Bremer and Jhon Lucumi at the back.

The proposed switch reflects the manager's willingness to adapt, and the need to find a system that gets the best out of his squad. Kolo Muani and Woltemade offer different qualities, and playing them together could add a new dimension. The defensive reshuffle is also a key part of the plan.

(Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Juventus's struggles have put Spalletti under pressure, and the defeat to Lazio has intensified the scrutiny. The manager's ability to find the right formula will be crucial in the coming weeks. The fans' patience is wearing thin, and results must improve.

The 3-5-2 system could provide more balance, but it also carries risks. The wing-backs will have a lot of ground to cover, and the back three must be solid. The tactical tweak is a gamble, but one that could pay off.

Spalletti's experience will be vital in navigating this difficult period, and the players must respond. The club's expectations are high, and the manager knows what is required. The next match will be a test of the new approach.

articles.title: Texans mailbag: Will Houston move a receiver before NFL's trade deadline? What is best RB rotation?
articles.summary: Insider Jonathan M. Alexander fields questions about potential changes to the Texans' starting lineups and possible trade-deadline moves in this week's mailb...
articles.body:
The Houston Texans have won two consecutive games, further fueling the idea that maybe, just maybe, they can turn things around.

The next quarter of their schedule, with games against the Giants, Chargers, Browns and Colts, is fairly pedestrian.

As a reminder, I do a mailbag every Wednesday. To ask a question, use the form below, send me an email at jonathan.alexander@houstonchronicle.com or send me a message on X.

Some questions may be lightly edited for brevity or clarity.

Q: Is there a reality where Houston opts to ride Woody Marks and Jawhar Jordan as RB1 and RB2, respectively, because they're better scheme fits?

JMA : No. I think David Montgomery still fits, and the Texans will try to make it work. After all, they invested a substantial amount in him, both in draft capital and with his contract.

The hope for the Texans is that, with the improvement of the offensive line and a different approach to the offense - pass-first - things will open up in the running game.

Montgomery is also still lethal at the goal line. He leads the Texans in rushing touchdowns. I do think Marks could get the majority of the carries, but I see no world in which Montgomery is RB3.

Jordan was placed on the practice squad injured list Wednesday, so he may not figure into the rotation for a while.

Q: What do you make of our (run-pass option) looks? In theory, it's one of the ways to help the run game, right?

JMA : It's a good wrinkle for this offense, especially considering fewer teams are doing it right now. When fewer offenses are using RPOs, as was the case 10 years ago, fewer defenses are preparing for them.

Just the threat that the Texans might pass, and teams' desire to defend against it, is helping the running game.

Adding RPOs to the fold shows the adaptability of offensive coordinator Nick Caley.

JMA : DeMeco Ryans often pointed to Blake Fisher's improvement this summer. The Texans are comfortable with Fisher starting if a player is injured.

I'd assume that if Trent Brown and Braden Smith aren't on the roster next year, the Texans would give Fisher a shot. But I don't think that's guaranteed. As of now, they like the role he's in.

As for Rankins, players have said he'd make a good coach. But he hasn't said that's what he wants to do.

Q : Why are there still five tight ends on the roster?

JMA : I'm assuming it's because they like the tight ends on their roster. They've used all five this season. And rookie Marlin Klein is viewed as a long-term project, as he always has been.

Q: More Marvin Harrison Jr. this week and beyond?

JMA : That's the plan. The Texans spent a second-round pick on Harrison, so the expectation is that he'll be a big part of this offense now and in the future.

There's an acclimation period, though. He'll need to fully learn the playbook before his snap count increases. After the game, he was asked how much of the playbook he knew. His response: "Not even half."

I'd say give him four to five weeks before we see him fully immersed.

Q: Is the offensive line we have now finally our best five, or is there still a possibility it could change with Braden Smith returning?

JMA : The Texans' offensive line had its best performance Sunday, so it's hard to imagine the coaching staff making a change now.

On the other hand, if things start to go wrong, Smith becomes an option. That's why they signed him.

But as of now, the Texans view this offensive line group as their best five.

Q: How has switching from Jerrod Johnson to Jerry Schuplinski (as QB coach) helped C.J. Stroud?

JMA : I don't necessarily believe Jerrod Johnson was the problem. I just think having one primary voice in the room probably helps streamline communication. Also, Schuplinski has worked with Nick Caley for a decade, so he probably has more insight into and experience with Caley's offense than Johnson, who comes from the Shanahan-style West Coast offense.

I still think Johnson was a good coach and will make a good offensive coordinator if given the opportunity.

Q: The wide receiver room seems to be getting a little crowded. With the trade deadline not too far away, do the Texans move someone for depth at another position or a draft pick?

JMA : It's always possible, but I get the sense the Texans would rather keep their wide receivers. Injuries have happened in the Texans' wide receiver room every year since 2023. It's a long season. The Texans will have six receivers on their roster when they officially add Tank Dell.

Q: When fans can see that players are a step too slow, why does it take an injury for coaches to replace them? For example, Jawhar Jordan for David Montgomery, M.J. Stewart for Reed Blankenship, or Kamari Ramsey for Jalen Pitre?

JMA : First, I want to say I 100% disagree with replacing Jalen Pitre with Kamari Ramsey. Pitre is one of the most underrated players on the Texans' defense. He does things Ramsey isn't yet capable of. He's also one of the team's best communicators and one of its better tacklers.

He's been beaten by elite wide receivers, but that doesn't mean the Texans should bench him.

I wrote about Montgomery earlier in the mailbag.

All in all, I think it speaks to the fact that the Texans believe those players give them the best chance to win. Otherwise, they wouldn't have paid them so much.

Now, I do think it's debatable and fair to ask who fits Ryans' defense better: Blankenship or Stewart?

Q: Have there been any meaningful behind-the-scenes changes to special teams over the last couple of weeks, or is the unit simply playing better? Which position group do you think the Texans try to add to before the deadline? Is Jawhar Jordan going to play his way onto our 53-man roster soon?

JMA : It's a couple of things. No. 1, the Texans are healthier. I think adding M.J. Stewart and Dare Ogunbowale, the Texans' two best special teams players over the past three seasons, has helped, especially with communication.

The Texans also swapped out Marlin Klein for Brevin Jordan. Jordan nearly forced a fumble on special teams before the play was ruled dead.

And now Jake Hansen is back on special teams in a full-time role. Those players have all made careers on special teams, so having them certainly helps.

As for potential moves, I don't see any more right now. I think Harrison was the trade deadline move they were going to make.

Regarding Jawhar Jordan, I believe he'll be placed on the 53-man roster if he can carve out a role on special teams. But for now, he's on the practice squad injured list.

Q: In hindsight, what's the best and worst roster-management move (Nick) Caserio has made six games into the season compared to what was done during the offseason?

JMA : The worst move of the offseason might have been not going after Kenneth Walker III or not doing enough to improve the offensive line.

The best moves were probably the trades for wide receivers. In the past, Caserio has been hesitant to make a big trade like that. It speaks to the Texans' desperation to win a Super Bowl this season.

Q: Did you have a better time in London than Aaron Wilson?

JMA : Haha. Apparently. My trip was actually pretty nice.

Q: If the defense is better with M.J. Stewart, do we bench Reed Blankenship? Also, how are they going to fix the defense's problems in the middle of the field?

JMA : If the defense is, in fact, better with Stewart, then I don't think DeMeco Ryans would hesitate to start him. Ryans trusts him.

But I do think the Texans signed Blankenship because they feel he can add something they perhaps haven't gotten yet.

Q: Is the offense acknowledging they're a pass-first play style and leaning away from the run game?

JMA : The first part is correct, but the Texans aren't going away from the run. They're just using it to open up the passing game.

One important thing to know is that you have to be able to run the ball in January, when weather conditions are at their worst.

I recently wrote about this, and I'll link to the story here .

Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander

Q: Do you think we can trade for Jonathan Taylor or Saquon Barkley to help our run game?

JMA : No. I do not. For one, both running backs will cost more than the Texans are willing to spend. They already gave up a second-round pick in next year's draft. Barkley and Taylor could cost more.

Also, the Colts won't trade with the Texans. Chris Ballard told me that a couple of years ago when I interviewed him for a story on Caserio. Ballard is no longer in charge, but his No. 2 is now making the decisions.

I also don't think the running backs are struggling as much as the run blocking is.

Q: What is the biggest thing holding back this defense's playmaking? We know what this group can be because it is the exact same as last year.

JMA : Well, it's not the exact same. There are new pieces, and that has contributed to the communication issues. But the talent is just as great, which is why I wouldn't panic yet. There's time to improve. I look at the 2025 Baltimore Ravens as a case study of a team whose defense dramatically improved over the second half of the season.

Right now, teams have the Texans' defense figured out. So it's a combination of game planning, finding the right lineup and developing consistency.

Q: Why are (Kamari) Lassiter and (Derek) Stingley Jr. playing soft coverage 5 to 6 yards off?

JMA : It depends on what play the defense thinks the offense is running. Sometimes, the defense calls for playing off to prevent an explosive play or to bait the offense into doing something the defense wants.

The mistakes have been on third-and-short or third-and-medium. Those are the times a defense should have its cornerbacks press.

Q: At the one third mark of the season, what letter grades do you give the Texans offense, defense, special teams and coaching staff? Better yet, why those grades?

JMA : I plan to grade all units during the off week stay tuned for that.

articles.title: Former Alabama coordinator no longer head coach at Big Ten program
articles.summary: The former Alabama offensive coordinator was in his eighth season as a head coach in the Big Ten prior to Wednesday's news.
articles.body:
Former Alabama Crimson Tide offensive coordinator Mike Locksley is no longer the head coach at Maryland, per the program Wednesday . According to the program, the Terrapins and Locksley mutually agreed to part ways.

Locksley had served as the head coach at Maryland dating back to the 2019 season. In his eighth season, Locksley posted a combined record of 39-54 while at Maryland dating back to 2015, with the Terrapins currently sitting at 2-5 overall (0-4 Big Ten) so far this fall.

A former offensive coordinator at Alabama , Locksley was in Tuscaloosa for three seasons from 2016-18. Locksley joined the Crimson Tide in 2016 as an offensive analyst before officially joining the staff in 2017 as co-offensive coordinator and wide receivers coach, and was later promoted to Alabama's offensive coordinator a year later in 2018.

Under Locksley, Alabama's offense ranked No. 3 nationally in 2018 with an average of 45.6 points per game. The Crimson Tide finished that season as the national runner-up at 14-1 overall (8-0 SEC), losing only in the CFP title game to Clemson.

Locksley was also the winner of the 2018 Broyles Award, which is presented annually to the nation's top assistant coach.

articles.title: Jimmy Anderson set to retire from cricket at 44 years old after Lancashire snub new contract offer
articles.summary: Anderson has reportedly been informed that he will not receive a new contract with Lancashire leaving his cricketing future in doubt
articles.body:
England cricket great James Anderson will not be given a new contract with Lancashire County Cricket Club leaving the future of his playing career in major doubt.

Anderson was reportedly informed of Lancashire's decision not to award him a new contract for 2027 after a meeting with incoming director of cricket Paul Farbrace and new chief executive Richard Kenyon on Monday. After a tumultuous time on and off the field, Lancashire are planning a new direction for the club.

Last season, Anderson took 50 wickets at an average of 17 and was one of only seven bowlers in the County Championship 's Division Two to take 50 wickets or more in the campaign.

The 44-year-old's future is now in doubt with the Daily Mail reporting that he will choose to retire from the game rather than looking to continue on at a different county.

Anderson remains England's highest ever wicket taker after claiming a record 704 wickets in Test cricket before being forced into international retirement in 2024. He continued to play Lancashire, his home county and the one he has represented for 25 years, and was named captain for the 2026 season.

Amidst ongoing turmoil at the club off the field, Anderson oversaw Lancashire's worst finish in the County Championship since 1984 as the club finished second to bottom in the Division Two table with only two wins recorded. Lancashire are now in the process of a hard reset with Farbrace and Kenyon replacing former director of cricket Mark Chilton and former chief executive Daniel Gidney who both left the club at the end of the season.

Anderson made his debut for Lancashire in May 2002. Over the next 20 years he became the most skilled swing and seam bowler in the world and claimed 1,193 first-class wickets at an average of 24 as well as 358 wickets in one-day cricket and 71 in T20s.

Regarding the decision to move him on once again, Anderson's age plus the uncertainty over his fitness should he pick up an injury will have played a role in the decision from Farbrace and Kenyon not to renew his contract. There is no question over his continued ability as last summer showed he was one of the outstanding competitors with the ball in county cricket.

Anderson has previously dabbled in franchise cricket having played in two matches of The Hundred for the Manchester Originals in 2025 but it seems unlikey that he will go down this route again to further his playing career having previously revealed that he "hated every minute" of those two games.

Another option would be to move to a different county for the 2027 season but only time will tell if that is a route he will take or if cricket has already seen the final act of the legendary James Anderson.

articles.title: Quenton Nelson addresses future with Colts after Ballard firing
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts LG Quenton Nelson addressed his future with the team on Wednesday following Chris Ballard's firing.
articles.body:
With GM Chris Ballard now gone, left guard Quenton Nelson's future with the team is now up in the air if the Indianapolis Colts do decide to become sellers at the NFL trade deadline.

Nelson is currently in the final year of his deal and is set to become a free agent in the offseason.

If it were up to Nelson, he would like to remain with the Colts , although that decision is not only his to make.

"Yeah, I Iove it here," Nelson said on Wednesday, via The Athletic's James Boyd. "Met my wife here. Really appreciate and love this organization. It's been a long career here. And made a lot of friendships and bonds here that I don't take for granted."

In the statement Carlie Irsay-Gordon released after sharing the news that Ballard had been let go, she reiterated that even with this move, the Colts' goals for the 2026 season remain the same.

However, at 2-4, the season could begin to spiral quickly, at which point the Colts could look to trade away players -- like Nelson at the trade deadline, in an effort to begin building towards the future.

How these next few weeks unfold will go a long way in dictating what direction Indianapolis goes at the trade deadline.

Still playing at a very high level, keeping Nelson around for 2027 and beyond certainly would make sense. That said, for a team likely entering rebuild mode, does it make sense to pay top dollar to retain Nelson when there is a lot of work to be done elsewhere on this roster?

That is the question Irsay-Gordon and Ed Dodds will have to answer in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Bob Uecker’s family sends message to Brewers ahead of World Series
articles.summary: With the Milwaukee Brewers preparing for the 2026 World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, the team is looking to achieve the highest level for the first tim...
articles.body:
With the Milwaukee Brewers preparing for the 2026 World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, the team is looking to achieve the highest level for the first time in its history: winning the championship series. As the Brewers are in the World Series for the first time since 1982, the family of legendary broadcaster Bob Uecker sent a message to the fanbase and the team ahead of the big series.

Uecker started as a player with Milwaukee from 1962 to 1962, and after retiring from the game, he became a broadcaster for the team in 1971 and continued until 2024, compiling an iconic career. He would unfortunately pass away in January of 2025 at 90 years old and with the Brewers making it to the World Series, saying that the "day has come" for what Milwaukee fans have been waiting for.

"Generations of Brewers fans have held hope in their hearts, season after season, that someday this city would have its chance at another championship, the Uecker family wrote. "Milwaukee is special. Its people are special. Our team is special. We are filled with elation and pride, but also longing. A wish that Bob was here to see it, too. While we could never speak for him, this is certain: Milwaukee, the Brewers, and the fans meant everything to Bob."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

How Brewers fans kept Bob Uecker's spirit alive

The Uecker family's statement continued in shouting out the players on the Brewers, saying that they "carried the city with you every time you took the field, making memories that will last a lifetime." Further saying that Bob Uecker "would have been so incredibly proud of what you've accomplished.

The statement also expressed excitement for manager Pat Murphy, the coaching staff, the Attanasio family, and the current broadcast team for honoring Uecker.

Ending with the fans, the family said that they "kept Bob's spirit alive-through a laugh, a story, a cold beer, or a favorite call."

"We feel your love for him every day, and our family is forever grateful," the family wrote.

Game 1 of the World Series between the Brewers and Rays starts on Friday night.
